 Environment
App version: (please fill your exact version, e.g. 1.15.13)
OS:  Windows 11
Installation type: Desktop EXE
Frequency: Always after latest update

Actual Behavior
The app opens the previous project instead of the selected/new one
Creating a new session does not work correctly
Switching between windows still loads the old project
Application becomes unresponsive or does not react to commands
Multiple windows show the same stale state

 Expected Behavior
Each project should open independently
New sessions should start fresh without reloading old state
Window switching should reflect correct active project
App should remain responsive to user commands

 Additional Notes
Issue started immediately after the latest update
Restarting the app does not fix the problem
Behavior is consistent across multiple attempts and sessions
⚠️ Possible Impact
This issue breaks core workflow (project isolation + session handling), making the desktop app unreliable for multi-project usage.

> The highest-leverage fix here feels like preserving the real stop cause all the way up the stack.
> 
> If a registered tool name parsed but args did not and `finishReason=length`, that is not an `invalid tool` event, it's `tool_call_truncated`. Once that gets misclassified, every recovery layer is reasoning from the wrong premise.
> 
> I'd propagate a typed truncation receipt with the tool name, attempt number, and whether the retry was auto-admitted or human-approved; otherwise subagents can burn budget re-proving the same truncation forever.

I agree with you. I encountered this problem last weekend as well—the subagent used up my entire budget in just one night.

I ended up with my own solution/workflow.

Just in case anyone could be interested (or it could inspire improvements to existing opencode ecosystem):

  - I use a separate tmux session for Opencode. In a spare monitor when I have one.
  - Then I write my prompts directly in neovim and get the answer in place throug my own "filter" implementation.
  - I can see the reasoning etc... in the spare monitor (when I have it) or switching to the Opencode session.
  - The tool include a --qa modifier to keep the original prompt in place.
  - I use it mostly with the --qa in a logbook-style file. But I can call it from other buffers / sessions to get code snippets in place, ask for a report of what we've done today, etc...

The tool is available at [https://www.npmjs.com/package/agentp](https://www.npmjs.com/package/agentp) . Now also includes two additional tools (ocmux to easily switch between projects/servers) and tgagentp (still in early stage) that let me to keep working/brainstorming through a Telegram bot when I am away.

Suggestions / colaborations are welcome (repo is linked at npm). Also if you do/know a more mature alternative, please let me know.

# Solution: Resolving VS Code and OpenCode Terminal Keybinding Conflicts

The issue occurs because VS Code globally intercepts certain shortcuts — such as `Ctrl+P` (Go to File) and `Ctrl+F` (Find) — even when the terminal is focused. This prevents CLI/TUI applications running in your terminal, like OpenCode, from receiving those inputs.

To fix this, you can configure VS Code to bypass its global shortcuts and pass those keys directly to the active terminal shell.

---

### Solution: Update your VS Code `settings.json` 

The cleanest way to fix this is to add the conflicting commands to the `terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell` array with a minus `-` prefix. This instructs VS Code to skip its own internal command when the terminal is active.

1. Open the Command Palette in VS Code (`Ctrl+Shift+P` or `Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS).
2. Type and select: **Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)**.
3. Paste the following configuration block inside the outer curly braces `{ }` of your `settings.json`:

```json
{
  "terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell": [
    "-workbench.action.quickOpen",                // Fixes ctrl+p and ctrl+e
    "-workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility",  // Fixes ctrl+b
    "-workbench.action.togglePanel",              // Fixes ctrl+j (hides terminal)
    "-workbench.action.quickOpenRecent",          // Fixes ctrl+r
    "-workbench.action.showAllSymbols",           // Fixes ctrl+t
    "-actions.find",                              // Fixes ctrl+f
    "-workbench.action.terminal.focusFind",       // Fixes ctrl+f inside terminal
    "-workbench.action.gotoLine",                 // Fixes ctrl+g
    "-workbench.action.closeActiveEditor",        // Fixes ctrl+w (closes tab)
    "-workbench.action.terminal.killEditor",      // Fixes ctrl+w in editor terminals
    "-editor.action.selectAll",                   // Fixes ctrl+a
    "-workbench.action.files.newUntitledFile",    // Fixes ctrl+n
    "-editor.action.quickFix",                    // Fixes ctrl+.
    "-workbench.action.zoomOut",                  // Fixes ctrl+-
    "-editor.action.rename"                       // Fixes f2
  ],
  "terminal.integrated.allowChords": false        // Prevents ctrl+k from waiting for a second chord key
}
